kind: A screen with one seed on the laptop's GPU: practice with feedback on multi-hop lookups, where a model may write anything before its answer and only the answer is checked; the test bed's stack and its Transformer of hop_generalization.json, each after its training on 1 to 4 hops.
why: Daniel asked for a model that reasons with chains of thought in its own words, without template-written answers and without a teacher model, and drew the loop: tasks generated and verified, attempted by the model, graded, kept where it solves a quarter to a half of them, the generator improved from the solve rate. Here programs play the helper models of the drawing. A hop task is answered by following a chain of names; between the query's '=' and its digit a model can write the names of the chain (?zt=mx=qa=7), each a lookup of one hop, so a chain of thought fits the task's own syntax and no program writes it. Trained on direct answers, the models have never seen such a chain: if practice makes them write one and get further, the chain of thought was learned from reward alone.
loop: experiments/practice_loop.py: every round 16 tasks at the current number of hops, verified (the answer follows from the line; the query is a name), 8 attempts each written as streams (a stack) or windows (the Transformer) at temperature 1.0 up to a newline or 48 bytes; reward 1 if the last byte before the newline is the answer; the solve rate moves the hops by a staircase (above a half +1, below a quarter -1), starting at 4; a GRPO step (rewards minus the group's mean over its spread, on the written bytes; Adam at 3e-5, gradients clipped at 1) on the tasks whose attempts disagree; 300 rounds; seed 0.

arms.practice-stack: hop-stack's averaged weights after its 12,000 updates
arms.practice-tf: hop-tf's averaged weights after its 12,000 updates

measure: Before and after practice, practice_loop.py --evaluate 1 2 3 4 6 8 12 16 --evaluate-tasks 200: greedy answers with room to think (up to 48 bytes), the accuracy of the last byte, the share of answers that write at least one name, the mean bytes; and the rounds' log: solve rate, hops, share of attempts that write a name.
reading: Read only for arms whose base learned the task by hop_generalization.json's mark (mean accuracy of at least 0.80 over 1 to 4 hops). (a) Practice works if an arm's accuracy at 8 hops after practice is at least 0.20 above its own before. (b) A chain of thought emerged if after practice at least half of an arm's answers at 8 hops write a name, and those answers are more accurate than the arm's answers without one (both reported). (c) The stack practises further than the Transformer if after practice its accuracy at 8 hops, and at 16, is at least 0.10 above the Transformer's with the 95% intervals apart. One seed, synthetic: a screen of the practice loop and of chains of thought learned without a teacher, not a claim about reasoning in language.
seen_before_recording: Three practice rounds of the 30-update smoke model (solve rate 0, nothing learned) that checked the loop end to end, and tests/test_practice_loop.py. No trained model has practised.

amendment.change: If no arm of hop_generalization.json learns the task in 12,000 updates (by its amendment of the same time: if hop-loop's mean over 1 to 4 hops is also below 0.80), practice-stack and practice-tf start from the averaged weights of hop-stack-24k and hop-tf-24k after their 24,000 updates instead, and run after those two are scored. The loop, the measure and the reading stay as registered: an arm is read only if its base learned the task by the mark, now at 24,000 updates. If hop-loop learns the task in 12,000 updates while hop-stack and hop-tf do not, neither arm can be read by the reading, and practice waits for a further amendment written before it runs.
amendment.seen_before_amendment: No practice has run. hop_generalization.json's scores at 1 to 4 hops of hop-stack and hop-tf and, by mistake, their accuracies past 4 hops (listed in that record's amendment); nothing of hop-loop's scores.
